messages:
leah.nguyen: Quick idea — we should split onboarding checks into two layers: (1) fast runtime-smoke at PR/ingest time to catch obvious kernel/IO breakage, and (2) full offline fidelity/eval that runs asynchronously. The smoke needs to be cheap (few inferences) but meaningful across variants (fp16, q4, cpu fallback).

jordan.cho: +1 on the split. Question: how cheap is "cheap"? running even 3 samples across 4 variants spins up a lot of transient containers. cost vs signal tradeoff. :thinking:

samir.patel: We ran a small experiment last month — 3 prompts x 5 steps x 3 seeds covers a lot of kernel mismatch cases. We also saw nondeterministic failures due to CUDA non-determinism on a subset of models; that argues for multiple seeds in the smoke.

leah.nguyen: Good call on seeds. Proposal for smoke: 3 prompts (safety, long-context, streaming), 3 repetitions, run on canonical variants: hosted-gpu(fp16), dedicated-gpu(q4), cpu. Keep time budget < 60s per job. If any run fails or output diffs beyond gross sanity thresholds, mark model as "needs-attention".

olivia.kim: How do we define "gross sanity thresholds"? exact match is impossible. maybe check: model returns tokens, no immediate OOM/crash, logits not NaN, and top-1 token exists (non-empty). Then schedule full eval.

jordan.cho: Also add a tiny perf probe: measure single-token latency and compare to expected profile. If token latency > 3x baseline, flag for runtime review. That helps catch bad kernel selections / fallback paths.

samir.patel: For the compatibility artifact, we should emit a small compat-matrix JSON artifact that lists variants tested, seed hashes, GPU driver/kernel, and pass/fail codes. Something like:
```
{
  "model_id": "m-abc",
  "variants": ["fp16-hosted","q4-dedicated","cpu"],
  "driver": "nvidia-530.30",
  "results": {"fp16-hosted": "pass","q4-dedicated": "fail_kernel_mismatch","cpu": "pass"}
}
```
This will be consumed by model-registry and the console.

leah.nguyen: Nice. That artifact boundary is important — it keeps onboarding logic decoupled from runtime decisions. We should agree on canonical result codes (pass, flaky, fail_exact_diff, fail_crash, fail_perf).

olivia.kim: Ownership question: who owns the smoke harness? eng-ml builds prompts and thresholds, runtime team owns orchestration + infra where it runs. @runtime-team (cc @runtime-bot) — can runtime expose a lightweight endpoint that accepts a model tarball/id and runs the smoke with configurable variants?

runtime-bot: Note: runtime team acknowledged. See RFC follow-up in #eng-runtime. We can provide a "rbi run-smoke" endpoint, but limits on concurrent bursts required (quota).

jordan.cho: Another tradeoff: doing more offline eval (longer, thorough) before admitting into registry reduces post-deploy regressions but increases time-to-availability. We should allow a fast-path for trusted partners/whitelisted models.

leah.nguyen: Agreed. Design: default path = smoke -> if pass, model is "admitted-limited" (can be used in dev & staging); full-eval must complete before "prod-admitted". Partners can request expedited full-eval via priority queue.

samir.patel: Implementation detail: the smoke should run deterministically where possible (set seeds, disable nondet kernels), but we still capture logs for RNG state if available. Also add a kludge: if a variant is flaky (pass/fail across seeds) mark "flaky" not hard-fail. That avoids blocking benign nondet issues.

olivia.kim: UI visibility: console needs to show compat-matrix with a timeline and an action button "request re-run" and "open runtime ticket". ops needs link to logs and the exact command used.

leah.nguyen: Example CLI to kick smoke (for design doc):
```
rbi run-smoke --model-id m-abc --variants fp16,q4,cpu --prompts smoke_small.json --reps 3 --timeout 60s
```
Outputs: compat-matrix JSON + per-run logs + perf probes.

jordan.cho: Final nit: ensure metrics emitted for false-positive rate of smoke (how often smoke passes but full-eval fails). We'll track that and iterate on thresholds. :white_check_mark:

leah.nguyen: Action items: 1) I will draft an RFC with proposed thresholds + artifact schema. 2) @runtime-team to confirm API and quotas. 3) @samir.patel to run a 100-model sampling and produce flaky/pass stats. Back in a week?

samir.patel: I'll start the sampling job today.

runtime-bot: Created ticket RUNTIME-2543 for smoke endpoint + quota design.
